lines_of_business: BCBSM and BCN; Medicare Advantage use when CMS rules not fully developed
effective_or_revised: Current Policy Effective Date: 11/1/25 (library metadata lists 11/1/2022)
criteria_location: Medical Policy Statement (p.1) and Inclusionary and Exclusionary Guidelines pp.2-3; conservative measures defined in two starred footnotes (* for limb and non-pneumatic, ** for trunk/chest). 24 pages total.
procedures_covered: Non-pneumatic compression appliances for limb (Koya Dayspring)

logic.top_level: pathways: limb nonprogrammable, limb programmable, non-pneumatic limb, trunk/chest
logic.exclusions_or_contraindications: Exclusions: limb pumps in 'all situations not mentioned above' experimental; head/neck experimental.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: The use of lymphedema pumps and appliances to treat the trunk or chest is limited to individuals with: • Lymphedema beyond the upper and lower extremities; and • Have failed conservative therapy**; and • Have failed therapy with lymphedema pumps and appliances to the upper and lower extremities only.
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: Conservative therapy** is itself defined to include a 4-week trial of E0650/E0651, which is also the third criterion; they overlap.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: *Conservative measures: a four-week trial of conservative therapy demonstrating failed responses to treatment is required.
Elevation where appropriate / Manual lymphatic drainage (where available)
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: Conditional requirements: when not appropriate/available, the component is waived but the chart must show why.

requirement_kinds.quote: The four-week trial of conservative therapy must include all of the following: Regular and compliant use of an appropriate compression bandage system or compression garment; Regular exercise; Elevation of the limb
The garment may be prefabricated or custom-fabricated but must provide adequate graduated compression starting with a minimum of 30 mmHg distally.
At least four weeks of regular, daily, multiple-hour home usage of the E0650 or E0651 after careful, in-person fitting, training and supervision
Manual lymphatic drainage (where available) and self-manual lymphatic drainage (MLD) for at least 30 minutes per day
Evaluation of diet and implementation of any necessary change; Medications as appropriate (e.g., diuretics ...); Correction (where possible) of anemia and/or hypoproteinemia

documentation that the individual has unique characteristics that prevent satisfactory pneumatic compression with single-compartment or multichamber nonprogrammable lymphedema pumps (e.g., significant scarring)
Lymphedema beyond the upper and lower extremities
Pneumatic compression pumps and appliances for the head/neck are experimental/investigational.

thresholds.quote: starting with a minimum of 30 mmHg distally
for at least 30 minutes per day

time_windows.quote: a four-week trial of conservative therapy

time_windows.what: home nonprogrammable pump trial for trunk
time_windows.quote: At least four weeks of regular, daily, multiple-hour home usage

definitions_that_change_meaning.definition_quote: (1) sufficient pressure at the lowest pressure point to cause fluid movement, and (2) sufficient pressure across the gradient ... The compression used must not create a tourniquet effect at any point.

extraction_hazards: Criteria hinge on star-footnotes (* and **) placed after the bullets, distinct definitions per footnote that overlap (** repeats the compression definition).
Policy history boxes and 'Current Policy Effective Date' vs metadata mismatch.
Medical Policy Statement says non-pneumatic limb 'established' but the title lists Koya Dayspring while BCBSFL calls it investigational.
interesting_structures: Non-pneumatic devices are covered, unlike BCBSFL and Cigna.
Two different conservative-therapy definitions (limb vs trunk).
No diagnosis staging, no continued-use rule, no venous ulcer indication.
Evidence statement states 'clinical input supports' trunk pump use.

fit_to_tree.why: Compact all-of lists with numeric anchors (30 mmHg, 4 weeks, 30 min), but conditional 'where appropriate/available' items and overlapping footnote definitions.
